Symptoms of food allergy are noted in Box 26-2.
The definition of allergy has been broadened to encompass 
any immunologic reaction to a component of food resulting in 
adverse symptoms and now includes reactions to foods that 
include the following:
•	 Reactions that elicit production of specific IgE
•	 Reactions that result from release of inflammatory media-
tors in response to IgE produced against nonfood materials 
such as inhaled pollens or latex
•	 Reactions that result from inflammatory mediators re-
leased from granulocytes such as eosinophils in the di-
gestive tract
•	 Food protein enteropathies due to proteins in milk or soy
•	 Food-associated disease such as gluten-sensitive enteropa-
thy (celiac disease), which has an immune component
